categories.main_business_segments: Deere & Company operates through four primary business segments: Production & Precision Agriculture (PPA), Small Agriculture & Turf (SAT), Construction & Forestry (CF), and Financial Services (FS). PPA focuses on large-scale crop production equipment and technology; SAT serves dairy, livestock, high-value crop, and turf customers; CF provides construction, roadbuilding, and forestry machinery; and FS offers financing solutions for equipment purchases and leases.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced manufacturing processes, digitalization, automation, and precision technologies across its equipment portfolio. Key technologies include global navigation satellite systems, telematics, on-board sensors, machine learning, autonomy, and the John Deere Operations Center™ digital platform. Manufacturing is optimized through process improvements, robotics, AI-driven analytics, and a global footprint that locates production near key markets.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Deere's primary customers are production-scale farmers (corn, soy, small grains, cotton, sugarcane), dairy and livestock producers, turf and utility operators, construction contractors, roadbuilders, and forestry companies. Major end markets include agriculture, turf care, construction, infrastructure, and forestry, with a significant portion of sales to large, mechanized farming operations and commercial construction firms.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with major sales in the U.S. and Canada, and significant presence in Western Europe, Brazil, Latin America, Australia, Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. Sales and support are organized around four regions: Africa/Asia/Middle East, Europe/CIS, Latin America/South America, and U.S./Canada/Australia, with manufacturing and distribution facilities worldwide.
categories.supply_chain_position: Deere operates primarily as an original equipment manufacturer (OEM), positioned downstream in the supply chain by delivering finished equipment, technology solutions, and aftermarket services directly to dealers and end customers. It also provides parts, engines, and components to third parties and supports its products with a global parts and service network.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities center on the Smart Industrial Operating Model and Leap Ambitions, emphasizing automation, autonomy, digitalization, lifecycle solutions, and Solutions as a Service (SaaS). R&D investments target intelligent equipment, precision agriculture, sustainability, electrification, and digital platforms to enhance customer productivity, profitability, and sustainability. The company is also focused on expanding aftermarket and support capabilities and integrating advanced technologies across all segments.
categories.revenue_model: Deere generates revenue primarily through the sale of equipment, parts, and technology solutions to dealers and end customers. Additional revenue streams include aftermarket services, precision technology upgrades, and financial services such as retail and wholesale financing, leasing, and extended warranties. The company is increasingly pursuing recurring revenue models through SaaS and digital solutions.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include AGCO, CNH Industrial, CLAAS, Kubota, The Toro Company (agriculture/turf), and Caterpillar, Komatsu, Volvo, Hitachi, Doosan, and others (construction/forestry). Deere is a global leader with strong brand recognition, particularly in North America, and competes on product performance, technology, quality, distribution, and customer service. The company faces competition from both established OEMs and emerging technology-focused entrants.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2025, Deere reported $45.7 billion in net sales and revenues, with net income of $5.0 billion. The company experienced a decline in sales and profitability compared to 2024, driven by challenging market conditions, especially in large agriculture. Despite the downturn, Deere maintains a large global scale, strong cash flows, and a history of structural profitability, with ongoing investments to support long-term growth and innovation.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Deere emphasizes delivering greater customer value through integrated equipment and technology solutions that enable higher productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Its differentiation lies in advanced precision technologies, digital platforms (John Deere Operations Center™), robust dealer and support networks, and a lifecycle approach to customer needs. The company positions itself as a leader in smart, connected, and sustainable equipment, helping customers 'do more with less' and adapt to evolving industry challenges.
